title: §.VIII: Omitting "improbant secus docentes" is tautology-avoidance; German prototype sub specie; like omissions already in Invariata witnesses
pass_a_gloss: But as to the other mutation or rather the omission of these Words in the Variata And they reject those who teach otherwise although we confess that words so expressed are not read there yet in the several Articles of any Confession whatsoever the same or similar words must necessarily be understood as implied: For he who positively confesses something in a Confession always denies and rejects that which stands otherwise; so that the omission of those words is to be held merely as an avoidance of Tautology and certainly can introduce no Substantial mutation. I pass over as to the prior mutation that in the prototype Exemplar of the Invariata Confession as the German distinctly shows the Article was expressed thus Dorsche not denying it cited page 183: Concerning the Lord's Supper etc. they confess that the Body and Blood of Christ are truly present under the species of bread and Wine; which of itself especially at that time could easily be doubted by no one to have smelled of Pontifical Transubstantiation. Whence also this Article consisting of those words is reported by all the Historiographers of the Augsburg Confession to have been simply admitted by the Pontificals. But as to the latter mutation it cannot be unknown that a similar indeed much more prolix rejection is found omitted in the Invariata exemplars of the Augsburg Confession in Chytraeus and Caelestinus compared with each other as to Article XIII and XVIII which Omission nevertheless did not prevent either Exemplar from always being held and still today being held as genuine by the Theologians of the Invariata Confession; and that in very many Articles for example in 3 4 6 7 11 14 18 19 20 21 from the very first framing of the Augsburg Confession no rejection of contrary teachings was added and yet it was nevertheless to be understood as implied.
pass_b_english: As for the other change — or rather the omission in the Variata of And they reject those who teach otherwise — we admit those exact words are not read there.
Yet in every article of any confession the same sense, or something like it, must be understood: whoever positively confesses a point always denies and rejects what stands against it.
So the omission is only an avoidance of tautology; it can introduce no substantial mutation.

I pass over this further note on the prior change: in the prototype exemplar of the Invariata as the German plainly shows, and Dorsche does not deny it page 183, the article was expressed thus — Concerning the Lord's Supper they confess that the body and blood of Christ are truly present under the species of bread and wine — which at that time could easily smell of pontifical transubstantiation by itself.
Hence the historiographers of the Augsburg Confession report that the pontificals simply admitted this article in those words.

And as for the later omission, it is no secret that a similar — indeed much longer — rejection is missing in the Invariata exemplars of Chytraeus and Caelestinus when Article XIII and XVIII are compared; yet that omission never kept Invariata theologians from treating either exemplar as genuine then or now.
In many articles besides — 3, 4, 6, 7, 11, 14, 18, 19, 20, 21 — no rejection of contrary teaching was added even at the Confession's first framing, and yet it was still to be heard as implied.
source_text: Ad mutationem verò alteram quod attinet, seu potius omissionem Verborum horum in Variata: Et improbant secus docentes, etsi verba sic expressa inibi haud legi fateamur, in Confessionis tamen cujuscunque Articulis singulis subintelligi vel eadem, vel similia, videri necessariò debent: Qui enim positivè aliquid in Confessione fatetur, ille id semper, quod secus se habet, diffitetur ac improbat; Ut proinde omissio verborum istorum, Tautologiae duntaxat evitatio habenda sit, certè Substantialem mutationem nullam inducere queat. Taceo, quod ad priorem mutationem attinet, in prototypo Exemplari Invariatae Confessionis (prout id Germanica disertè ostendit) Articulum ita fuisse expressum, (non diffitente Dorscheo, cit. pag. 183.) De Coena Domini &c. fatentur, Corpus & Sanguinem Christi, sub specie panis & Vini, verè adesse; id quod Transubstantiationem Pontificiam per se, istô praesertim tempore, redoluisse, nulli facilè dubium esse potest. Unde etiam à Pontificiis Articulus hic, dictis verbis constans, simpliciter admissus fertur ab Historiographis Augustanae Confessionis omnibus. Quod ad posteriorem verò mutationem attinet, ignotum esse haud potest, & similem, imò prolixiorem multò improbationem omissam deprehendi in Augustanae Confessionis invariatae Exemplaribus Chytraei & Caelestini, inter se collatis, quoad Articulum XIII. & XVIII. (Quae tamen Omissio nihil prohibuit, quò minus ab Invariatae Confessionis Theologis utrumque Exemplar pro genuino habitum semper sit, hodièque habeatur.) & in plurimis Articulis e.g. in 3. 4. 6. 7. 11. 14. 18. 19. 20. 21. ne a prima quidem Aug. Confessionis adornatione improbationem contrariorum adjectam, nihilominus subaudiendam fuisse.
